title: Lesson 7: Templates That Scale: Parameterized Prompts You Reuse With Different Inputs
description: Parameterized prompts: a fixed frame written once with a few named variable slots filled fresh each run, why the stable frame beats re-deciding the prompt every time, and the judgment about when a task earns a template at all.

questions.question: In a reusable prompt, where does most of the value come from?
options: The fresh material you paste into the blanks each run
The length of the template, which signals the effort behind it
The fixed frame, written once and reused unchanged
The number of slots, which covers more possible variations
questions.explanation: The frame, the role, format, tone, and criteria, is what makes the output the same shape run after run. The filling changes by nature, so the consistent part is what earns the template its keep.

questions.question: Why must the fresh input be clearly separated from the standing instructions inside a template?
options: So the model treats it as data for this run, not as a rule
So the template file stays shorter and much easier to store
So the slot can be left empty on runs with no new facts
So the review step can be dropped for that particular run
questions.explanation: A marked boundary tells the model which text is an instruction and which is today's material. Blend the two and a value can be read as a rule, changing the shape of the output.

questions.question: A task recurs often, but its shape changes from run to run. What is the right call?
options: Build the template anyway and force the task to fit the frame
Skip it, because a frame that keeps changing will not hold
Add more slots so every variation has its own placeholder
Build a separate template for each variation the task might take
questions.explanation: A reusable prompt pays off only when a task recurs and its frame stays stable across runs. When the shape keeps shifting, the fixed part is never reused, so the setup is wasted.
